source.title: Refusal Reads Only a Slice of What the Model Knows: Harm-Keyed Routing and Its Exceptions Across Model Families

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper applies a refusal-direction difference-of-means and Arditi-style weight ablation to new models, measuring refusal and capability outcomes. It also reports additional causal interchange and activation-level ablation tests.
record.gate_note: The paper’s causal tests include weight-folded refusal-direction ablations, activation-level projection-out, and interchange patches. Reported values used only to select layers or construct controls are not included as standalone findings. Cited results from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: Section F applies the Arditi harmful-minus-harmless difference-of-means direction as a weight-orthogonalizing edit to OLMo-3, Qwen2.5 and Llama-3.1 instruct models. It reports refusal rates and capability readouts before and after. Section G.1 ablates single refusal directions in the reasoning model GPT-OSS-20B, and Section 4 compares the base proto-refusal direction with the instruct gate. Most of the rest (moral-subspace interchange sweeps, refusal vs moral-judgment geometry) bears on a related construct, not on a version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors' central claim is that refusal, a fresh post-training gate in a narrow channel, reads a low-rank harm slice rather than the broad moral subspace on OLMo-3 (causal) and GPT-OSS (correlational). Llama reads broadly and Qwen is unresolved. Rank-one removal is clean on OLMo and Qwen, only halves Llama's refusal at a judgment cost, and no single direction coherently removes refusal on GPT-OSS.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference refusal direction and an Arditi-style orthogonalizing weight edit, but tests new models and layers and adds behavioral capability measures, activation-level projection-out, interchange rank sweeps, and reasoning-model ablations.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by model family and intervention: weight-folded edits versus activation-level projection-out differ; Llama retains more refusal and loses moral-judgment accuracy; GPT-OSS single-direction outcomes depend on the direction’s position and coherence filter. Qwen’s read-axis verdict is unresolved at n=19.

fits_no_version.finding: On OLMo-3, refusal's transfer from nested moral-subspace patches plateaus near 0.22–0.27 while moral-judgment transfer climbs to 0.66. On Llama, refusal transfer (0.85) matches judgment (0.79); Qwen is indeterminate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: What content feeds the refusal direction (harm percept vs broad moral content) varies by model family.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal-decision and moral-judgment-decision directions at the decision token have low cosines (0.10, 0.32, 0.08) against nulls. The refusal direction projects 0.10 into the moral subspace.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal direction is geometrically separate from moral-judgment representations.

fits_no_version.finding: The harm direction lies mostly outside the moral subspace (in-subspace fraction 0.11 in reasoning distills).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The harmfulness representation is largely distinct from moral-foundation content.

record.problems: The causal interchange rank sweep is on OLMo alone; Qwen’s read-axis sample is 19 twins and indeterminate. GPT-OSS harm-reading evidence is correlational, with its causal interchange test held; its refusal-direction ablation is reported as unsuccessful or incoherent. Llama’s edit has a moral-judgment cost. The activation-level OLMo projection-out does not remove refusal. General capabilities beyond the reported moral-content and moral-judgment measures are not assessed, and the harmless-request refusal-induction test is not run.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Excluded reported measurements that do not directly test the listed versions, including decision-site participation ratios, head-write attribution, GPT-OSS prefill reversibility behavior, and harm-direction steering that measures moral judgments rather than refusal.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts. General capabilities beyond moral probes and judgment. All-layer activation ablation as in the original.
Released abliterated checkpoints and broader capability benchmarks.
Entire version: no jailbreak or adversarial-training tests.
No multi-direction or cone ablation that removes refusal; the cone reading on GPT-OSS is inferred from failed single-direction ablation.
Cross-language and cross-family transfer; base-to-instruct is only a cosine, with no causal transfer test.
Entire version: training method and timing are not varied; the checkpoint tracking shows when the gate forms, not whether training decides removability.
Only GPT-OSS-20B is tested by ablation; there is no weight-edit test on reasoning models.

missing.what: Moral probe accuracy (1.0) and effective dimension (5) unchanged after ablation on Qwen and Llama, not only OLMo.
Persona-shift compliance under refusal ablation: OLMo 0.75→1.00, Qwen 0.90→1.00, Llama 0.70→0.95.
Llama half-strength ablation: judgment drop 0.083 while refusal is still 0.90; full-strength drop 0.146.
OLMo judgment accuracy after layer-16 refusal projection-out: 0.750 vs baseline 0.742, no cross-effect.

record.verdict_notes: Most of the paper's headline results concern what feeds refusal, not the refusal direction's causal role, so they go under fits_no_version. Moral judgment is not treated as V5's harmfulness judgment. OLMo baselines differ by request set (0.25, 0.575, 0.62). The OLMo judgment figures conflict between F.1 (0.73→0.75) and F.2 (0.75→0.79). This is a single-author preprint, pre-registered.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test adding the refusal direction to induce refusals on harmless requests, and does not assess broad general capabilities beyond the reported moral-content and judgment measures.
The weight-edit battery covers three instruct families, not every released model; GPT-OSS is tested with other ablation directions, not this weight-edit method.
No test of attacks suppressing the refusal direction or of training against its ablation.
The study does not establish a general geometric account covering all model families; Qwen’s read-axis result is explicitly unresolved at its sample size.
The harmfulness/refusal separation is measured most directly on GPT-OSS; the reported reply-inversion steering results measure moral judgments, not refusal behavior.
The paper measures base-to-instruct similarity for OLMo’s proto-refusal and gate, but does not test cross-language transfer or transfer of one extracted direction across model families.
Training-stage tracking of refusal precursor and gate alignment is on OLMo-3; the study does not vary refusal-training method or timing experimentally across models.
Reasoning-model tests are limited to GPT-OSS direction ablations and correlational harm-loading/reversibility results; the paper does not run the OLMo-style causal rank sweep on GPT-OSS.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: OLMo-3 and Qwen2.5 weight-edit ablations; OLMo moral measures
reader_labels.reason: The specified weight edit removes measured refusal on OLMo and Qwen while reported OLMo moral probe, subspace dimension, and behavioral judgment remain stable (R1–R3, R5–R7).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Llama weight-edit ablation and OLMo layer-output projection-out
reader_labels.reason: The Llama edit leaves substantial refusal and reduces moral-judgment accuracy; OLMo activation-level projection-out increases rather than removes refusal (R4, R9, R10).
